summary: Iter274: tested provider backup buying, provider health hiding stock, bot country list and address-only numbers, the MultiTEL GB search, the Travel eSIM shop (API + UI) and regression pages. Backend: 12/12 pytest checks passed, plus node checks with fake Infobip/MultiTEL modules. Results: if the first provider fails and the other sells, the order comes back with _provider set to the other provider and _failover set; if both fail, null comes back. A retry on the same provider returns _retriedNumber. If the backup provider is down, it is never called. A provider is marked down after 2 failed health checks and number-catalog then drops it from options() and sold(). moreCountries has 52 entries, all multitel/infobip, every type has best() level <=1, none businessOnly or request. botNeedsAddress AU/local=true, GB/mobile=false, allCountries=[US,CA]. The GB mobile texting search returns 10 MultiTEL +44 numbers (1 MultiTEL search used). Travel eSIM: 187 zones, every price is exactly 3x cost, UK = 1/5/10/20 GB at $6/12/18/45. The dry-run order debits $6 and returns active with an LPA code. Orders are per user, an unknown or missing offerId returns 404, and Bob gets 402 on a too-expensive plan with his balance unchanged. UI: the japan search filter, the no-match message, the UK zone with 4 plan cards, checkout, paying, and the order showing 'Ready to install' with the install block all work, and the wallet dropped $6. International Texting, Texting Number, Number lookup and Get a number all load. Code review of the SMS 3-try logic, voicemail after a failed forward, dialWithBackup, and the telnyxPaidCheckout short-circuit with providerOfOrder found the logic as described.

minor.issue: Permanent errors (invalid number, blocked destination) are also retried 3 times with 1.5s/3s waits, which adds about 4.5s before the customer sees the error. The 'attempts: 3' log entry and the 'We tried 3 times' message are also written even if an error is not retryable.

MultiTEL/Infobip detection uses isMtSearched/isIbSearched, which are in-memory 'searched' sets. If the process restarts, or another active slot handles the request between search and checkout, a MultiTEL/Infobip number falls through to the Telnyx path and its buy fails (refunded). This is an edge case.

recordResale hardcodes provider 'telnyx', and the replacement doc keeps the old provider. Replacing a MultiTEL/Infobip number therefore records the wrong provider. This is not in this round's scope but is related to the 'save real provider' change.

The transactions chatId is String(req.webChatId) but the travelEsims chatId is the raw value, so the two can differ in type. There is also no per-user lock on POST /orders: a double submit makes 2 orders, though the UI disables the button while busy.

issues: The zone grid shows only the first 40 of 187 countries with no 'type to see more' hint. Users may think only A-B countries exist.
Orders show no purchase date or validity days left.
Dry-run orders show an empty 'QR shows here' box with nothing to mark them as preview orders (the banner at the top does say simulated).

action_items: Optional: only retry SMS sends on transient errors (5xx or timeout), not on permanent ones like invalid or blocked numbers
Optional: store the provider of searched numbers in Mongo (or check the number's provider by country/type) so checkout survives a restart
Optional: Travel eSIM: add a hint when the list is truncated at 40, show order date and validity, and normalise the chatId type in the transactions doc
critical_code_review_comments: buyWithBackup only fails over to the other provider when its option is level 0 and not a request. Address-only (level 1) numbers therefore never fail over, which matches the 'no paperwork' rule.
moreCountries is a getter, so the bot list updates as provider health changes. With both providers down it correctly returns 0 entries.
The voicemail-after-failed-forward path is guarded by _vmAfterForward, the voicemail feature being enabled, and canAccessFeature. It is ordered after the off-hours fallback, which is correct.

dialWithBackup only retries when the leg is bird, CALL_ENGINE_BACKUP_TRUNK is set, the destination is not SIP, and the cause is not busy, unallocated or a number change. CALL_ENGINE_BACKUP_TRUNK is not set yet, so this path is currently inactive.
seed_data_creation: None kept. I made 2 Travel eSIM dry-run orders for Alice (pytest + UI). Both orders and their transactions were deleted and the $6 each was credited back (Alice is at $353.97). The order tes_9dc2de19-a45 already existed (from E1) and was left alone.
context_for_next_testing_agent: MultiTEL login works now; I used 1 GB mobile search. Bird: the catalog was fetched once (6h cache) and 0 lookups were used. The provider backup tests use fake modules loaded into Module._load from a temporary file in /app/js (the /tmp/fo_test.js pattern). Watch out: a fake multitel api() returning {} makes MultiTEL look down after 2 ticks. The nav testid for Number lookup is nav-lookup.
